extracted.intended_audience: school and college administrators, Title IX coordinators, compliance officers, and institutional legal counsel responsible for implementing Title IX grievance procedures
extracted.subtask_short: Title IX grievance procedures for schools
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements for recipients (elementary, secondary, and postsecondary institutions) to design and implement Title IX grievance procedures, including evidence access, credibility assessment, standards of proof, and procedural safeguards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal opportunity to access relevant, not otherwise impermissible evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must provide each party an equal opportunity to access the evidence that is relevant to the allegations and not otherwise impermissible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two options are expressly allowed: (1) provide access to the underlying relevant evidence; or (2) provide an accurate description of such evidence. If the recipient initially provides only a description and a party requests access to the evidence, the recipient must provide access. Both options require giving the parties a reasonable opportunity to respond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable opportunity to respond to evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must give parties a reasonable opportunity to respond to the evidence or to an accurate description of the evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasonableness means the parties can meaningfully respond. Because evidence volume and nature vary, the Department declines to set examples or fixed timeframes. The opportunity to respond generally takes place at the end of the investigation after evidence is gathered, but recipients may allow responses at other points in the investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to take reasonable steps to prevent and address unauthorized disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must take reasonable steps to prevent and address a party's unauthorized disclosure of information and evidence obtained solely through the grievance procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department does not prescribe specific measures because what is reasonable varies by circumstance. Steps could include informing parties of expectations and consequences for unauthorized disclosures or using software that restricts further distribution. Disclosures for purposes of administrative proceedings or litigation related to the complaint are explicitly authorized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interaction with FERPA — disclosure override where necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: When Title IX regulations require disclosure of evidence that would otherwise be covered by FERPA, the Department's constitutional and GEPA overrides apply to permit disclosure to parties and their advisors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FERPA generally defines 'education records' and gives parents/eligible students the right to inspect records. Certain education-record materials may be redacted where possible, but if Title IX requires disclosure of evidence from education records, recipients must disclose under the applicable overrides. Section 106.6(g) preserves parents' legal rights to act on behalf of students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process for assessing credibility (decisionmaker questioning)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must create a process for assessing the credibility of parties and witnesses when credibility is in dispute and relevant to evaluating allegations, and that process must enable the decisionmaker to question parties and witnesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department requires a process that allows the decisionmaker to ask questions to adequately assess credibility; mere review of evidence is not sufficient. Recipients have discretion to design the process (including single-investigator models or other non-quasi-legal approaches) taking into account due process, administrative structure, educational community, and applicable law. Additional process may be required in individual cases to satisfy constitutional due process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidentiary relevance standard for questions and evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Any questions a decisionmaker asks and any evidence used in the grievance procedures must be relevant and not otherwise impermissible under §§106.2 and 106.45(b)(7).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This evidentiary filter applies to the process for assessing credibility to avoid retraumatizing or irrelevant inquiry. Recipients must exclude impermissible evidence and ensure questions comply with the evidentiary standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility regarding live hearings, cross-examination, and single-investigator models
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients are not required to use live hearings or questioning by an advisor; they may implement live hearings, decisionmaker-questioning processes, or single-investigator models as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For elementary and secondary schools, live hearings and advisor questioning are generally not required because of student age/development; recipients may nonetheless choose to use them (with flexibility to tailor procedures). Postsecondary institutions have distinct provisions for live hearings in sex-based harassment cases. Recipients must ensure chosen formats satisfy §106.45(g) when credibility is at issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of age, developmental level, and potential trauma
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients should account for the age and developmental level of students and the potential for questions to be traumatizing when designing processes to assess credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department declines to prescribe exact methods but will offer technical assistance. Questioning must still comply with the evidentiary relevance standard. Recipients may adapt processes (e.g., avoid direct party questioning) for younger students and work with parents to facilitate procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard of proof — default to preponderance of the evidence (with all-comparable-proceedings exception)
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must use the preponderance of the evidence standard to determine whether sex discrimination occurred unless the recipient uses the clear and convincing evidence standard in all other comparable proceedings, in which case it may elect clear and convincing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department retained the July 2022 NPRM standard. The rule preserves recipient flexibility and does not require the same standard across student and employee proceedings as the 2020 amendments did. Courts have upheld preponderance as constitutionally permissible in school disciplinary Title IX contexts. Some commenters advocated sliding scales or differential standards by severity, but the Department declined to adopt those approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equitable treatment of complainants and respondents
rubrics_metrics.description: Grievance procedures must treat complainants and respondents equitably.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a general requirement of §106.45(b)(1) and underpins the suite of procedural safeguards the Department identifies to ensure fairness and reliability in determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient discretion to dismiss complaints in specified circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may dismiss a complaint in four different circumstances, including when allegations, even if proven, would not constitute sex discrimination under Title IX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section §106.45(d) describes dismissal grounds; dismissals are part of ensuring that grievance procedures address allegations that fall within Title IX's scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to the parties of the allegations
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must provide notice to the parties of the allegations against a respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice is a prerequisite to allowing parties to prepare responses and participate meaningfully in the grievance process; see §106.45(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grievance procedures required before imposition of disciplinary sanctions
rubrics_metrics.description: The recipient's grievance procedures must be followed before imposing any disciplinary sanctions against a respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sanctions may only be imposed if it is determined that the respondent engaged in prohibited sex discrimination (see §106.45(h)(3) and (h)(4)). This protects due process and ensures procedural protections are exhausted prior to sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective evaluation of all relevant evidence and exclusion of impermissible evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must objectively evaluate all relevant evidence and exclude certain types of evidence deemed impermissible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections §106.45(b)(6) and (7) require impartial evaluation and list categories of evidence that must be excluded; this works in tandem with burdens on the recipient to investigate thoroughly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient bears burden to conduct an investigation and gather sufficient evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: The recipient has the burden to conduct an investigation that gathers sufficient evidence to reach a determination about whether sex discrimination occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section §106.45(f)(1) places responsibility on the institution (not on the parties) to collect evidence necessary for reliable outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal opportunity to present witnesses and other relevant, non-impermissible evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Each party must have an equal opportunity to present fact witnesses and other inculpatory and exculpatory evidence that are relevant and not otherwise impermissible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section §106.45(f)(2) requires parity in opportunities to present evidence, supporting a balanced fact-finding process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decisionmaker impartiality — no conflict of interest or bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisionmakers must not have a conflict of interest or bias for or against complainants or respondents generally or an individual party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section §106.45(b)(2) is intended to reduce the risk of prejudgment and ensure fair determinations; OCR enforcement may address abuses of discretion or failures to comply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption that respondent is not responsible until determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Grievance procedures must include a presumption that the respondent is not responsible for the alleged conduct until a determination is made at the conclusion of the grievance procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section §106.45(b)(3) codifies this presumption to protect due process and fairness in adjudication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy protections for parties and witnesses
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must take reasonable steps to protect the privacy of parties and witnesses during the grievance procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section §106.45(b)(5) requires privacy safeguards to minimize harm and protect participation; privacy must be balanced with disclosure obligations under the regulations and applicable overrides.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training requirements for decisionmakers
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisionmakers must receive training, including on serving impartially by avoiding prejudgment of the facts at issue, conflicts of interest, and bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section §106.8(d) outlines training expectations to help ensure impartial application of grievance procedures and reduce biased outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals — minimum parity and allowed bases
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must offer the parties an appeal that, at a minimum, is the same as the appeal offered in all other comparable proceedings; postsecondary institutions must offer appeals for bases including procedural irregularity or bias that would change the outcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section §106.45(i) requires parity in appeals; §106.46(i) provides specific postsecondary appeal bases (procedural irregularity, bias/conflict of interest, etc.). Institutions may offer additional appeal bases if they apply equally to all parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to adopt additional provisions so long as applied equally
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may adopt additional provisions as part of their grievance procedures provided those additional provisions apply equally to the parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section §106.45(j) permits flexibility and local tailoring of procedures, with the constraint of equal application to all parties to maintain fairness.
